doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Learning stage patter: Grover Kemble and comedy records
summary: Asked how early rock and roll helped his stage manner, he cites Grover Kemble, comedy records and watching Carson.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What are you nuts? Five sharps? We don’t do that. Well you’ve always had a gift of gab and that’s a compliment. And I’ve wondered, Bucky was not very verbose. He let his music speak. Did the early rock & roll experience you had help you get comfortable on stage interacting with the audience?

No you know actually in New Jersey I worked with a guy named Grover Kemble. And Grover was a — still is, is like a Jersey presence. He was a guy who’d go out and play the guitar and he would constantly egg the band on, I mean egg the audience on. And it was always so interesting. I’m just going to turn that off there so we don’t get anymore dings.
I’m going to turn off something here myself, hold on.
We’ll get rid of that, the heat fan came on.
